In [[geometry]], the '''triaugmented truncated dodecahedron''' is one of the [[Johnson solid]]s ({{math|''J''{{sub|71}}}}).  Of them, it has the greatest surface area and volume for a given side length, as well as the greatest numbers of edges and vertices; it is tied for the greatest number of faces with [[gyrate rhombicosidodecahedron|{{math|''J''{{sub|72}}}}]], [[parabigyrate rhombicosidodecahedron|{{math|''J''{{sub|73}}}}]], [[metabigyrate rhombicosidodecahedron|{{math|''J''{{sub|74}}}}]], and [[trigyrate rhombicosidodecahedron|{{math|''J''{{sub|75}}}}]]. As its name suggests, it is created by attaching three [[pentagonal cupola]]s ({{math|''J''{{sub|5}}}}) onto three nonadjacent [[decagon]]al faces of a [[truncated dodecahedron]].
